name: Multispectral Imager
description: Captures several visible and infrared color bands.
whyItMatters: More bands help distinguish water, plants, and urban areas, but create a large data and power demand.

name: Fluxgate Magnetometer
description: Measures the strength and direction of local magnetic fields.
whyItMatters: It uses little power and data while revealing how a planet's magnetic environment behaves.

name: Compact Imaging Spectrometer
description: Splits light into many narrow color bands to identify materials.
whyItMatters: It can identify minerals and surface materials, at the cost of more processing and downlink capacity.

name: Thermal Infrared Radiometer
description: Measures heat emitted by land, ocean, or atmosphere.
whyItMatters: Temperature maps support climate and hazard studies without the data volume of a detailed imager.

name: Small Space Telescope
description: A compact optical telescope for observations above Earth's atmosphere.
whyItMatters: A stable view enables faint-target science, but precision pointing is essential.

name: Planetary Context Camera
description: A compact camera for planetary flybys and lunar surface context.
whyItMatters: It can capture a useful target view with modest spacecraft resources, though it returns less detail than a large imager.

name: Space Radiation Monitor
description: Counts energetic particles near the spacecraft.
whyItMatters: It tracks a hazard to astronauts and spacecraft while using very little power and downlink.

name: Premium Hyperspectral Mapper
description: A premium high-band-count mapping instrument with an unusually high catalog price.
whyItMatters: It produces exceptional material detail, but its cost, power, mass, and data demands make it a deliberate budget trap.

name: Solar-Wind Analyzer
description: Samples the speed and density of charged particles flowing from the Sun.
whyItMatters: It complements particle counts with the flow that drives space-weather disturbances.

name: Atmospheric Limb Sounder
description: Measures atmospheric layers at the edge of Earth's horizon.
whyItMatters: Its lower data rate can add atmospheric context without the full burden of a second imager.
